questions.q: A screenplay introduces its hero walking into a café and ordering coffee. What's the main problem?
choices: The scene has no Midpoint
It needs voiceover
The first action could be anyone's: it doesn't define the character
Cafés are clichés
questions.explain: A first action should be something only this character would do.

questions.q: Which screenplay introduction line follows the advice in this lesson?
choices: JANE (34) straightens every picture frame in the waiting room, then glares at anyone who touches one.
JANE (34), brown hair, 5'6", blue jeans, white shirt.
Jane enters.
JANE, our heroine, is very complex.
questions.explain: Essence and attitude, shown through action, beat an inventory of looks.

questions.q: In Raiders of the Lost Ark, why does the film keep Indiana Jones's face hidden until he cracks his whip?
choices: To save money on the actor
To hide a twist about his identity
Because it's a flashback
To build mystery, then reveal him at a moment of decisive competence
questions.explain: The reveal is timed to his first defining action, so face and skill arrive together.

questions.q: Molière keeps Tartuffe offstage until Act 3. What does the delay achieve?
choices: It shortens the play
The household's arguments about him make us eager to judge him, and his first gestures expose him
It hides that he's a ghost
It follows the unity of time
questions.explain: A delayed entrance turns the audience's curiosity into a question the entrance answers.

questions.q: In The Silence of the Lambs, Clarice is warned at length before meeting Lecter. Why is his calm, courteous manner so effective?
choices: It contradicts the build-up, making him stranger and more frightening than the monster we imagined
It shows he's innocent
It's a save-the-cat moment
It's a false Midpoint
questions.explain: Others' talk builds expectation; the gap between reputation and reality is the point.

questions.q: Harry Lime appears about an hour into The Third Man, revealed in a doorway by a light from a window. What technique is this?
choices: In medias res
A kicker
A delayed entrance built on other characters' talk about him
Cross-cutting
questions.explain: The film is full of talk about Harry before he appears, so the audience has built him in their heads first.

questions.q: A profile of a chef opens: 'Maria Lopez, 52, has worked in kitchens for thirty years.' What would this lesson suggest?
choices: Add her education
Move her age to the end
Start with a quote from a critic
Open on her doing something characteristic, in a scene
questions.explain: A profile lede is a character introduction: scene and action rather than résumé.

questions.q: The Godfather introduces Michael at the wedding, in uniform, insisting he's not like his family. Why is that useful?
choices: It's a red herring about his identity
It sets a starting point the whole film measures his change against
It's a delayed entrance
It's a kick-the-dog moment
questions.explain: An introduction can show who someone is now, so we can see how far they travel.

ideas: A character's first action works as a thesis that the rest of the story tests.
Letting other characters talk about someone before they appear builds expectation, and the gap between reputation and reality becomes the point.
Keeping a character offstage for acts, or for most of a film, can make their first appearance the event the audience is waiting for.
